subject.title: [Bug] Docker sandbox container name collision across multiple instances on same host

question: Should OpenClaw accept workspace-scoped non-shared sandbox runtime identity as the security boundary fix for co-hosted instances, including the documented one-time runtime reset on upgrade?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but the fix changes persistent sandbox runtime names, registry keys, and cleanup semantics across multiple backends, so maintainer intent is needed before landing.

options.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
options.body: Land the active candidate after explicitly accepting that old non-shared runtimes are recreated under workspace-scoped identities and removed by recreate or prune.

options.title: Require migration or doctor repair
options.body: Ask for a migration or doctor path if preserving old non-shared runtime state matters more than a one-time reset.

options.title: Split backend policy
options.body: Pause the candidate fix if Docker, browser, SSH, and skills workspace identity should not all move under one scope-key policy.

recommendation.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
recommendation.body: Land the active candidate after explicitly accepting that old non-shared runtimes are recreated under workspace-scoped identities and removed by recreate or prune.

likelyOwner.reason: The history pass shows the broadest prior work on sandbox lifecycle, OpenShell, security, and docs in this owner boundary.
